predecessors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
predecessors.text: Galicia and Lodomeria as carved in 1772, without the city of Kraków

successors.name: Second Polish Republic
successors.text: Galicia and Lodomeria: Zator and Auschwitz, part of Little Poland and all of Galicia

ledger.x: 5 August 1772: the First Partition gives Austria Galicia; 'The crown land was established in 1772, after the First Partition of Poland', 'The name of the newly created realm, selected by the Habsburgs in 1772'.
1786: Bukovina 'became part of Galicia as the Bukowiner Kreis'.
1809: 'Austria was forced in the Treaty of Schönbrunn to cede all of its third partition gains' to the Duchy of Warsaw, 'including Zamość'.
1809: 'Austria was also forced to cede the Tarnopoler Kreis' to Russia.
1815: 'the Congress of Vienna returned Ternopil and a few other territories to Austria'.
1846: 'In 1846, Austria annexed the Free City of Cracow', which became the Grand Duchy of Kraków and gave the realm its ceremonial title with the Duchies of Auschwitz and Zator.
19 October 1918: the eastern regions are claimed by the West Ukrainian People's Republic after the dissolution of Austria-Hungary; it 'briefly declared the independence of Eastern Galicia'.

14 November 1918: Galicia 'joined to Poland'; 'In late 1918, Eastern Galicia became a part of the restored Republic of Poland'; the fate of Galicia was settled by the Peace of Riga on 18 March 1921 and the Treaty of Saint-Germain on 10 September 1919.
1918: the Kingdom's status 'remained unchanged until the dissolution of the monarchy in 1918'; Charles I (1916-1918) is the last ruler.

wars.name: First Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: Austria took 83,000 km2 and 2,650,000 people; the Sejm committee signed the treaty of cession on 18 September 1773.

wars.name: Third Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: After the Kościuszko Uprising (24 March 1794), the powers 'met on 24 October 1795 to dissolve the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth'; Austria took Western Galicia and Southern Mazovia.

wars.name: Austro-French war of 1809 (Treaty of Schönbrunn)
wars.outcome: Austria ceded West Galicia to the Duchy of Warsaw and the Tarnopoler Kreis to Russia; the Congress of Vienna returned Ternopil in 1815.

certainty.note: Partition treaty lines (1772, 1795) and the treaty of Vienna (1815); the page says the borders were stable from 1849 to 1918.
